summary: Phase A end-to-end testing complete. Backend: 15/15 pytest pass for FIR endpoint (full payload, BMI=27.7, status='WAITING_FOR_DOCTOR', visit_type, complaint_text), validation (422 on missing consulting_doctor_id, 404 on bad doctor, 403 on pharmacy/doctor/pro), legacy POST /api/patients (BMI null backward compat), PATCH BMI auto-recompute on height_cm and weight_kg, followup date-only (case has next_followup_date='2026-07-15' + next_followup_at='2026-07-15T03:30:00+00:00' UTC = 09:00 IST, reminder doc has scheduled_date+patient_phone+status='PENDING'), 422 on invalid/missing date, scheduler does NOT auto-COMPLETE (PENDING with past scheduled_at flipped to FAILED, never COMPLETED). Frontend: reception FIR form renders with all required data-testids, BMI auto-updates to 27.7 from 170cm/80kg, Referral name field appears on REFERRAL select and disappears on deselect, submission navigates to /reception/patients/{id}/timeline. Doctor FollowupTab uses type='date' input, confirmation contains the date. Doctor Reminders page shows date-only (e.g. '15 Jul 2026', '20 Aug 2026') — no AM/PM time. Pharmacy Reminders page renders without time format. No bugs found.
critical_code_review_comments: routers/patients.py:create_patient_fir — patient.bmi is computed but patient_doc still echoes all PatientIn fields including chief_complaint, visit_type, sources etc. These are arguably case-level attributes (visit_type already lives on the case). Storing them on the patient root could go stale on subsequent visits. Consider: persist only patient demographics + sources/referral on the patient; persist chief_complaint+visit_type only on the case. Non-blocking — current spec accepts the redundancy.

models.py:FIRPatientIn inherits PatientIn and re-declares consulting_doctor_id/chief_complaint/visit_type as required. Works but a cleaner approach is a fresh BaseModel composing PatientIn fields to avoid the implicit override pattern.
routers/cases.py:set_followup — datetime.combine + .astimezone(utc) is correct but timezone(timedelta(5h30)) is allocated on every call. Lift to module-level IST constant (one-line cleanup).

routers/cases.py:set_followup — reminder doc duplicates patient_name/patient_uid/patient_phone snapshotted at creation time; if the patient updates their phone, the existing reminder still holds the old number. Acceptable for short-window reminders but documented as a known limitation.

reception/NewPatient.jsx — submit() does `Object.keys(payload).forEach(k => delete payload[k] if '' or null)`. This deletes `chief_complaint` if user accidentally enters whitespace-only, but Pydantic will then 422. Could pre-trim and surface a clearer 'required' UI error before POST. Minor UX.
reception/NewPatient.jsx — `data-testid` is correctly applied to all interactive elements per spec. Good.
Scheduler test took 70-80s due to 60s tick interval; consider lowering interval in dev env via config or exposing a manual /admin/scheduler/tick endpoint to speed up E2E runs.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase A is fully verified and production-ready. Backend test file at /app/backend/tests/test_phase_a.py is reusable as regression for Phase B/C/D rounds — it spans patient FIR creation, BMI auto-compute, followup date anchoring, and scheduler invariant (never auto-COMPLETE). Note: the scheduler test sleeps up to 90s waiting for the 60s reminder_scheduler tick — keep that in mind for test budget. Main agent can wipe DB before Phase B testing without affecting this round's correctness.
rca of the issue: No issues to RCA — implementation matches spec exactly. BMI formula 80/(1.70^2)=27.68 rounds to 27.7; IST anchor 2026-07-15 09:00 +05:30 → 2026-07-15 03:30 UTC; FIR creates patient+case atomically and audit logs both rows with via='FIR' metadata; scheduler only writes status=SENT|FAILED in send_reminder() — no code path sets COMPLETED automatically (only the manual PATCH /reminders/{id} with status=COMPLETED does, which requires authenticated user action).
